red_flags.flag: A failed company, with creditors paid at 40 cents
red_flags.how: Answer it with a specific story from the file rather than a claim.

red_flags.flag: Five-month employment gap he has not settled on a way to describe
red_flags.how: Say what happened and what was done with the time in two or three factual sentences.

red_flags.flag: Currently self-employed, so no manager can be asked about him
red_flags.how: Show it through a story where the applicant made a commercial or people decision and carried others with them.

red_flags.flag: German grade of 2.1 that readers will not benchmark easily
red_flags.how: Point to the quantitative and academic evidence elsewhere in the file in one plain paragraph; no apology and no excuse.

red_flags.flag: Risk of reading as either self-flagellating or evasive about the shutdown
red_flags.how: Answer it with a specific story from the file rather than a claim.

kit_properties: Every number in every draft matches the Fact Sheet or a story's own numbers.
No draft names a person whose story marks them as not to be named.
No sentence uses any of these words: passionate, journey, pivot, failing forward, learnings, my baby, crushed it, impactful.

The goals essay names the short-term goal specifically: An operating role at a logistics or commerce company with real scale — a regional general manager or a head of operations for a business unit — in Germany or the Netherlands, where the unit economics are someone's actual job.
The leadership essay leads with "The per-drop price I set too low", or the Strategist says why another story is stronger.
The setback essay leads with "The afternoon I did eleven conversations", or the Strategist says why another story is stronger.
